decisions.reason: The source changes only the placard's viewing orientations; the spout remains independently oriented toward the baristas.
Displaying the same placard wording on both sides does not change the machine's beige body or green accents.
The placard orientation decision does not alter bowl capacity, depth, geometry, or enclosure-size constraints.
The source does not change the enclosure's thickness, overall size, or accommodation of the bowl wells.
Placard wording and viewing orientation do not affect whisk selection, positioning, mixing quality, or foam performance.
The client does not request a BOM revision or specify any changed component selection for the two-sided placard.
The passive placard orientation change does not alter electrical loads, power capacity, controllers, or overload protection.
The placard decision does not modify the dispensing mechanism, flow behavior, sequence, or texture-preservation constraints.
Showing placard wording to both viewing directions does not change splash targets or mitigation methods.
The source does not affect whisk removability, detachment, clearance, cleaning, or swapping behavior.
The placard's two-sided presentation does not alter bowl removal, swapping, or assembly-clearance requirements.
The general layout and CAD deliverable remains required unchanged; the specific placard design change is fully owned by the source Requirement.
